title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is an isolated sheet of the L-function notes. The neighbouring pages are Bourbaki drafts of Commutative Algebra ch. VII exercises and are unrelated. The setting is the geometric case. X is a curve, or more generally a scheme of finite type over a finite field. y is the generic point. E_y is an l-adic representation of the Galois group of the function field, i.e. a lisse Q_l-sheaf on an open U, extended by j_*. x is a closed point.

The usual local factor at x is det(1 - Frob_x t | E^{I_x})^{-1}, i.e. it uses the stalk (j_*E)_x. This is not additive in short exact sequences of E, because taking inertia invariants is only left exact.

Grothendieck considers forcing additivity, so that the L-function factors through the Grothendieck group:
- First define the local factor for absolutely simple E_y. He allows finite extensions of Q_l so that simple means absolutely simple. For such E the factor is (j_*E)_x.
- Then extend by linearity. Take a composition series of E with simple factors E^i and set E_y(x) := Σ_i (j_*E^i)_x as a virtual or semisimple object. The local factor of L_{E_y}(t) is then L_{E_y(x)}(t).

He then rejects this himself. The construction is not local in (E,x): it does not commute with an étale base change X'→X that has trivial residue extension at x.
- Such a base change does not change the inertia or decomposition group at x.
- It does shrink the global monodromy. So a globally simple E can become reducible on X', and the composition factors (hence the sum of their inertia invariants) change.
- Example: E simple globally but locally at x a nonsplit unipotent extension. Then dim E^{I_x} = 1 before base change. After a base change that makes E globally reducible, the sum over composition factors gives 2.

Conclusion: the 'right' local factor must depend only on the restriction of E to the decomposition group at x. The semisimplification of the global representation does not have that property. This is the reason one keeps the non-additive definition via j_* and inertia invariants, as in SGA 4 1/2 / SGA 5 and Deligne's Weil II.
errors: No mathematical error. The objection is correct: global semisimplification is not compatible with étale localization, whereas inertia invariants depend only on the local Galois representation. The remark is a sketch without an explicit counterexample.

ideas.what: Local factor at x of an l-adic sheaf defined via inertia invariants / stalk of j_*; non-additivity in exact sequences
ideas.modern_name: Local L-factor det(1 - Frob t | V^{I_x}); intermediate extension j_* for L-functions on curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Bourbaki exposé 279, 1964; SGA 5), Deligne (Weil II, Constantes locales)
ideas.where_published: Formule de Lefschetz et rationalité des fonctions L (Sém. Bourbaki 279); SGA 5

ideas.what: Attempt to make L additive via composition series of absolutely simple factors, rejected because it is not étale-local
ideas.modern_name: Semisimplification vs. locality of local factors; local factors depend only on the restriction to the decomposition group

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard design consideration for defining local L-factors of non-semisimple l-adic sheaves: additivity versus locality, resolved in favour of j_* and inertia invariants. It is well understood in the literature (SGA 5, Deligne). The page is a short self-correcting remark, with nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'facteurs locaux dans L_{E_y}(t)' likely reads 'facteurs locaux de L_{E_y}(t)'.
'E_y^{i*}(x)' is plausibly E^i_{y*}(x), i.e. the stalk at x of j_* of the simple factor E^i_y; the subscript in the image resembles '2' but is surely y.
'de nature locale' fits the image ('ne sont pas de nature locale en (E,x)').

In the last line the struck-out word after 'étale' is likely 'sur X' (deleted and moved to the end), and the parenthesis reads '(à ext. résiduelle triviale) sur X', with an earlier word above 'résiduelle' struck out.
